overview: AI agents are scaling software development productivity, as OpenAI’s CodeRabbit claims 20x output gains.
Anthropic’s new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models target harder technical tasks, with faster inference and lower costs.
DeepMind demonstrates AI‑assisted formal verification of the Signal protocol, highlighting both promise and current limits.

top.title: CodeRabbit scales agentic software development and ships 20x more
top.summary: OpenAI’s CodeRabbit uses its models to manage AI‑generated code, enabling a single engineering team to ship software at roughly twenty times the previous rate, showcasing agentic development pipelines.

top.title: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
top.summary: OpenAI’s Control Room provides a centralized dashboard to monitor model workloads across its research infrastructure and can halt runs instantly when safety or security concerns emerge.

top.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
top.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, designed for demanding technical problems; the models claim better coding, reasoning, vision, faster output, and have solved several open scientific challenges during testing.

top.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
top.summary: Google DeepMind used its AlphaProof Code framework to formally verify key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol, confirming its security and illustrating AI‑aided formal verification’s potential.

top.title: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
top.summary: Anthropic is proceeding with an IPO despite market volatility, aiming to set a valuation below earlier $1.5 trillion targets, while investors gauge the health of the broader AI boom.

top.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
top.summary: Anthropic’s Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 launch with improved coding, reasoning, vision, lower pricing, and faster inference; the release notes ongoing concerns about evaluating covert capabilities and recursive self‑improvement.
